lesson.scenario: A session service uses one Bloom filter per tenant partition to reject definitely absent session IDs before reading its authoritative database.
entities: Requests a session by tenant and session ID
Owns the read path and treats the filter as a negative cache
Maps tenant IDs to filter and database partitions
Answers definitely absent or maybe present for one partition
Authoritative source for session existence and payload
Builds new generations from snapshots and committed inserts
connections: read only when filter says maybe

steps.title: Partitioned filters are ready
steps.narration: The service keeps a small Bloom filter for each database partition rather than one globally contended filter.
steps.outcome: Filter memory and rebuild work are isolated by partition.
steps.invariant: The directory must route a request to the filter generation built from the same logical database partition.

steps.title: Route the request
steps.narration: A request for tenant-7 session s77 resolves to partition P3 before the service probes the filter.
steps.outcome: The service selects P3-g18 without broadcasting to every filter.
steps.invariant: Partitioning reduces memory and rebuild blast radius but requires consistent routing metadata.

steps.title: Definite miss skips the database
steps.narration: The P3 filter finds at least one zero bit for s77, proving that s77 was not inserted into this generation.
steps.outcome: The service returns without spending a database read.
steps.invariant: A Bloom filter is useful here only if the system prevents false negatives.

steps.title: Maybe present requires verification
steps.narration: Session ghost42 maps only to set bits. That is not proof of existence, so the service reads the authoritative database.
steps.outcome: The database exposes a harmless false positive; the client still receives a correct 404.
steps.invariant: Never treat maybe present as an authoritative positive.

steps.title: Real positive reaches the database
steps.narration: Session s42 also produces maybe present, and the database confirms the row and returns its payload.
steps.outcome: The filter saves negative reads while preserving database authority for positive answers.
steps.invariant: Bloom filters optimize absence-heavy workloads; they do not replace the source of truth.

steps.title: Rebuild instead of clearing bits
steps.narration: Deletes and rising occupancy trigger a background rebuild because clearing a shared bit could create a false negative for another key.
action: build P3 generation 19 from snapshot @ LSN 1040
steps.outcome: Generation 18 remains readable while generation 19 catches up.
steps.invariant: Standard Bloom filters cannot safely delete individual keys by clearing shared bits.

steps.title: Publish a healthier generation
steps.narration: After replay reaches the database checkpoint, the directory atomically switches P3 to a larger, lower-occupancy filter.
steps.outcome: False-positive pressure falls without interrupting the request path.
steps.invariant: Publish a rebuilt filter only after it includes every committed insert through its cutover checkpoint.

production.scenario: A public package registry edge rejects requests for never-published package versions before touching the catalog primary.
components: npm, pip, and Maven clients requesting package versions
Regional edge that terminates auth and package lookups
Black-box negative-membership gate loaded with published package coordinates
Authoritative package metadata and publish state
Worker that tails publish events and rebuilds the membership asset
Versioned object store for signed filter snapshots
Rolls out a new filter generation to every edge
flows: CI clients ask the registry edge for a specific package coordinate before any catalog read happens.
The edge asks the existence gate whether the coordinate is definitely unknown or worth confirming.
Only maybe-present coordinates reach the authoritative catalog primary for metadata and entitlement checks.
The catalog streams publish and unpublish changes so the membership asset follows authoritative state.
A builder compacts the latest catalog view into a versioned snapshot that edges can trust.
The release control plane tells every edge which snapshot generation is active in production.
A restarting edge reloads the latest approved snapshot before it resumes package traffic.
